lead: Meta Platforms / FB — the record crash everyone thinks they understand
smaller: Amazon / AMZN — the giant that answered with AWS
Tesla / TSLA — the record recall you fix by download
Bitcoin / BTC — the safe-haven claim gets one good day
why_lead: Repeat lead justified as a material update with a new angle. The 2022-02-03 lead ('the metaverse bill comes due') could cite only the after-hours reaction, framed the stock as value versus falling knife and named the 3 February regular session as the pending test. That session is now on the card (FB 237.76 USD, -26.39% 1-session, -26.66% 20-session) and newly published 3 February evidence changes the story from a spending scare to a contested diagnosis of the core business: biggest one-day drop ever (CNBC n0811); $232 billion record (CNBC n1141); the Apple diagnosis (WSJ $10 billion sting n1137; Macworld's iPhone alert n1133) versus the competition diagnosis (first-ever user shrink n1142; Zuckerberg on TikTok n1166); world tech contagion (Reuters n0842; card Nasdaq 100 -4.22%, Snap -23.60%, Pinterest -10.32% before their own results, VIX +2.26 pts to 24.35). The Social Signal is coverage reach and the competing record figures (Bloomberg $251 billion n0838, Business Insider nearly $240 billion n1149, CBS $237 billion n0868), local and foreign broadcast pickup (WPTV n0843, ABC n1134), retail explainers (Motley Fool n0882, Yahoo Finance n0879) and the Berkshire scoreboard (n0841). Analog: PayPal's worst-ever day (CNBC n0733) followed by a further -6.24% on the card, with an ownership-handover mechanism distinct from the 2022-02-03 'sellers into every bounce' wording. Smart money: $1 trillion of funds exposed (Bloomberg n0837), Buffett via TheStreet (n0793), NYT/Forbes bears (n0844, n0808) versus the data-divide bulls (Reuters n1153, CNBC n0809). Triggers: the 237.76 USD close, Friday's read-through from Pinterest's after-close beat (Reuters n0856) to the Apple-versus-TikTok diagnosis, and the 2Y (1.19%, +36 bps, bear flattening) ahead of the jobs report the White House warned Omicron could skew (n2022). No sentence, analog mechanism or trigger of the 2022-02-03 lead is reused; the $10 billion Apple figure recurs only through new 3 February headlines (WSJ n1137, Macworld n1133). Relation to other strictly earlier notes: 2022-02-01 GameStop and 2022-02-02 Alphabet leads are not repeated; PayPal (2022-02-02 and 2022-02-03 smaller) appears only as the Historical Analog with new card data.
why_smaller: Amazon / AMZN: new item, distinct after-hours comeback and pricing-power narrative, and the Meta lead's counterpart on the data divide — -7.81% to 2,776.91 USD in the 3 February session, then the after-hours surge on the cloud beat and Rivian gain (CNBC n0787), AWS +40% to $17.78 billion (Shacknews n0099), a $31 billion advertising business (CNBC n1128) on the data-rich side of Reuters' Big Tech divide (n1153), Prime up nearly 17% to $139 (CNBC n0784); breaks on GeekWire's $1.8 billion ex-AWS operating loss (n0788), the Rivian mark, cost-driven Prime hike (Reuters n1129) and Friday's pending session against the 2,776.91 USD close.

Tesla / TSLA: new item (not an item on 2022-02-01 to 2022-02-03), distinct brand-faith narrative — two recalls in a week (Reuters n1857 nearly 54,000 vehicles; Notebookcheck n1917 largest ever) answered by an over-the-air fix (Teslarati n1921, 817k cars), relative resilience on the card (-1.60% to 891.14 USD vs Nasdaq 100 -4.22%; +7.48% 5-session) and Morgan Stanley's revenue projection (Wccftech n1154); breaks on phantom-braking reports (Washington Post n1884), the -18.10% 20-session gap and the 891.14 USD close on the next heavy Nasdaq day.

Bitcoin / BTC: new item, distinct safe-haven/decoupling narrative — bitcoin +0.55% to 37,154.60 USD and ether -0.14% on the Meta crash day; religion and better-than-gold framing (The Conversation n0966, Barron's n1757); Stocktwits rolling out crypto trading (Reuters n1762) as retail-platform evidence; the Wormhole theft ($325 million, Elliptic n0943) and Jump Crypto's replacement of over $320M (The Defiant n0962); breaks on the listed proxies trading like tech (GBTC -3.60%, Coinbase -3.23%, Marathon -7.86%), the -13.79% 20-session gap and bailout dependence.
considered_not_chosen: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ (-12.03% to 56.74 USD, SOXL -13.60%; chipmakers n0796): an earlier draft item, replaced in independent review. It carried no attention evidence, repeated the daily-reset leverage caution already used in the 2022-02-01 GameStop lead and the 2022-02-03 Meta trigger list, and leaned on a meme-stock headline (The Edge Singapore n0836) that is a reprint of a headline already cited on 2022-02-01; the leverage read-through is a data point, not a new narrative.
Spotify / SPOT (-16.76% to 159.76 USD after results; BBC n1916, Tubefilter n0867): would be a third consecutive appearance (2022-02-01, 2022-02-03 smaller items) without a materially new catalyst.

Snap / SNAP (-23.60% to 24.50 USD) and Pinterest / PINS (-10.32%; 'results dazzle Wall St' n0856 vs sliding active users n1156): used in the lead as contagion data and as the Apple-versus-TikTok test; Snap's own results are covered only by an uninformative TechCrunch headline (n1161).
Ford / F (-3.59%; shares skid despite bullish outlook n0814; Rivian-boosted $17.9 billion n0813): the Rivian mark-to-market angle is covered in the Amazon item.
Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (+22.07% 5-session, +60.99% 20-session) and Robinhood (+21.88% 5-session): no own-date headline explaining the moves.

Not used: n1260 (Reuters 'Bank of England raises rates by most since 1995 even as long recession looms', stamped 2022-02-03) is contradicted by own-date coverage of the 3 February decision (a hike to 0.5%, n1259; a second consecutive hike, n0790; not enough for 4 officials, n1262) and describes a different, larger decision; recommended for exclusion. n0690 (Fortune, Tesla 'true worth $138 a share') not used because the headline gives no date context for a valuation figure. Ark adding Tesla (n0671) not used because its source label could not be attributed cleanly. Lagarde (n0102) and BoE (n1259) dropped for length; the lead's rate trigger rests on the card's 2Y.

Pending after the cutoff and not treated as outcomes: US January payrolls (referenced only via the White House warning n2022, without a date), the Putin–Xi meeting and Beijing Olympic opening, the RBA Statement on Monetary Policy, and the 4 February regular sessions of Meta, Amazon, Snap and Pinterest.
Feb 3-stamped items were checked for after-cutoff content; all cited ones describe 3 February sessions, after-hours results or events completed before 00:00 UTC on 4 February.
